rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.

WITH
bounds AS (
  SELECT
    date(min(txn_date)) AS min_date,
    date(max(txn_date)) AS max_date
  FROM customer_transactions
),
months AS (
  SELECT
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_date)) AS month_start,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_date), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
    0 AS rn
  FROM bounds
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    date(month_start, '+1 month'),
    date(month_start, '+2 month', '-1 day'),
    rn + 1
  FROM months, bounds
  WHERE date(month_start, '+1 month') <= date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', max_date))
),
tx AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    LOWER(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC) AS txn_amount,
    CASE
      WHEN LOWER(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC)
      WHEN LOWER(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw') THEN - CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC)
      ELSE CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC)
    END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
),
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM tx
),
cust_month AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', m.month_start) AS month_year,
    m.month_start AS month_start_date,
    m.month_end AS month_end_date
  FROM customers c
  CROSS JOIN months m
),
monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month_year,
    SUM(signed_amount) AS net_month_amount
  FROM tx
  GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)
),
grid AS (
  SELECT
    cm.customer_id,
    cm.month_year,
    cm.month_start_date,
    cm.month_end_date,
    COALESCE(mn.net_month_amount, 0) AS net_month_amount
  FROM cust_month cm
  LEFT JOIN monthly_net mn
    ON mn.customer_id = cm.customer_id
   AND mn.month_year = cm.month_year
)
SELECT
  g.customer_id,
  g.month_year,
  g.month_start_date AS month_start_date,
  g.month_end_date AS month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance: running sum of monthly nets up to this month
  SUM(g.net_month_amount) OVER (
    PARTITION BY g.customer_id
    ORDER BY g.month_start_date
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change is the net activity in the month
  g.net_month_amount AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance is the same as closing_balance (running total)
  SUM(g.net_month_amount) OVER (
    PARTITION BY g.customer_id
    ORDER BY g.month_start_date
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM grid g
ORDER BY g.customer_id, g.month_start_date

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages

WITH customer_master AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
),
months_2020 AS (
  SELECT '2020-01' AS month_label UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-02' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-03' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-04' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-05' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-06' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-07' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-08' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-09' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-10' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-11' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-12'
),
customer_month_population AS (
  SELECT cm.customer_id, m.month_label
  FROM customer_master cm
  CROSS JOIN months_2020 m
),
customer_monthly_txn_totals AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', ct.txn_date) AS month_label,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposit,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_withdrawal
  FROM customer_transactions ct
  WHERE ct.txn_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
    AND ct.txn_type IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', ct.txn_date)
),
monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    cmp.month_label,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(cmt.sum_deposit,0) - COALESCE(cmt.sum_withdrawal,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_customer_count,
    AVG(COALESCE(cmt.sum_deposit,0) - COALESCE(cmt.sum_withdrawal,0)) AS average_month_end_balance
  FROM customer_month_population cmp
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_txn_totals cmt
    ON cmp.customer_id = cmt.customer_id
    AND cmp.month_label = cmt.month_label
  GROUP BY cmp.month_label
),
highest AS (
  SELECT month_label, positive_customer_count, average_month_end_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT m.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count DESC, month_label ASC) rn
    FROM monthly_stats m
  ) WHERE rn = 1
),
lowest AS (
  SELECT month_label, positive_customer_count, average_month_end_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT m.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count ASC, month_label ASC) rn
    FROM monthly_stats m
  ) WHERE rn = 1
),
diff AS (
  SELECT
    h.average_month_end_balance - l.average_month_end_balance AS difference_between_averages,
    h.month_label AS high_month_label,
    l.month_label AS low_month_label
  FROM highest h CROSS JOIN lowest l
)
SELECT
  m.month_label,
  m.positive_customer_count,
  m.average_month_end_balance,
  CASE WHEN m.month_label = d.high_month_label THEN 'highest' ELSE 'lowest' END AS note,
  d.difference_between_averages
FROM monthly_stats m
CROSS JOIN diff d
WHERE m.month_label IN (d.high_month_label, d.low_month_label)
ORDER BY CASE WHEN m.month_label = d.high_month_label THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_cleaned AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    substr(txn_date,1,7) AS txn_date_ym,
    CAST(substr(txn_date,1,4) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(substr(txn_date,6,2) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month,
    txn_type,
    CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ABS(txn_amount) ELSE -ABS(txn_amount) END AS txn_amount_signed
  FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date_ym,
    txn_year,
    txn_month,
    SUM(txn_amount_signed) AS monthly_net
  FROM customer_transaction_cleaned
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date_ym, txn_year, txn_month
),
monthly_with_closing AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date_ym,
    txn_year,
    txn_month,
    monthly_net,
    SUM(monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_year, txn_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_year DESC, txn_month DESC) AS rn_desc
  FROM customer_monthly_net
),
most_recent_and_prev AS (
  SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.closing_balance AS recent_closing,
    COALESCE(p.closing_balance, 0.0) AS prev_closing
  FROM monthly_with_closing m
  LEFT JOIN monthly_with_closing p
    ON m.customer_id = p.customer_id
    AND p.rn_desc = 2
  WHERE m.rn_desc = 1
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN (CASE WHEN prev_closing = 0 THEN recent_closing * 100.0 ELSE (recent_closing - prev_closing) / prev_closing END) > 0.05
      THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0
    END
  ) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_with_recent_growth_gt_5_percent
FROM most_recent_and_prev

WITH months_present AS (
  SELECT
    DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS year_month,
    strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date) AS first_day_of_month,
    CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) = (
      SELECT MIN(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) FROM customer_transactions
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_earliest_month
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
-- normalize dates that are already ISO; keep only rows where txn_date is parseable as YYYY-MM-DD
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date_iso,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
-- for each month (from months_present) and each customer, compute cumulative sum of txn_amount for txn_date < first_day_of_month
cust_cumulative AS (
  SELECT
    m.year_month AS target_month,
    m.first_day_of_month AS first_day_of_month,
    t.customer_id,
    SUM(t.txn_amount) AS cumulative_balance
  FROM months_present m
  JOIN txns t
    ON t.txn_date_iso < m.first_day_of_month
  GROUP BY m.year_month, m.first_day_of_month, t.customer_id
)
SELECT
  m.year_month AS month_year,
  m.first_day_of_month AS as_of_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN coalesce(c.cumulative_balance, 0) > 0 THEN c.cumulative_balance ELSE 0 END) AS total_balance
FROM months_present m
LEFT JOIN cust_cumulative c
  ON c.target_month = m.year_month
WHERE m.is_earliest_month = 0
GROUP BY m.year_month, m.first_day_of_month
ORDER BY m.year_month ASC

WITH customer_daily_transactions AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(txn_date,1,10) AS date,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS daily_deposit_sum,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type != 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS daily_withdrawal_sum,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount WHEN txn_type != 'deposit' THEN -txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS daily_net_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id, date
),
-- generate running balance per customer per calendar date by cumulative sum over dates
customer_running_balance_by_date AS (
  SELECT
    cdt.customer_id,
    cdt.date,
    cdt.daily_net_amount,
    (
      SELECT SUM(cdt2.daily_net_amount)
      FROM customer_daily_transactions cdt2
      WHERE cdt2.customer_id = cdt.customer_id
        AND date(cdt2.date) <= date(cdt.date)
    ) AS running_balance
  FROM customer_daily_transactions cdt
),
-- compute 30-day rolling average of the running_balance for each customer/date,
-- using window that looks at current and prior 29 rows ordered by date.
-- Also count rows in the window to ensure at least 30 days are present.
customer_30day_rolling_avg_running_balance AS (
  SELECT
    crb.customer_id,
    crb.date,
    crb.running_balance,
    AVG(crb.running_balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY crb.customer_id
      ORDER BY date(crb.date)
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS rolling_30d_avg,
    COUNT(crb.running_balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY crb.customer_id
      ORDER BY date(crb.date)
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS rolling_30d_count
  FROM customer_running_balance_by_date crb
),
-- baseline month per customer = month of earliest date
customer_baseline AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(MIN(date),1,7) AS baseline_month
  FROM customer_running_balance_by_date
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- for each customer and month, compute the maximum of non-negative 30-day rolling averages
per_customer_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    substr(r.date,1,7) AS month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN r.rolling_30d_count >= 30 THEN CASE WHEN r.rolling_30d_avg < 0 THEN 0 ELSE r.rolling_30d_avg END END) AS customer_month_max
  FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_running_balance r
  JOIN customer_baseline b ON r.customer_id = b.customer_id
  WHERE substr(r.date,1,7) <> b.baseline_month
  GROUP BY r.customer_id, substr(r.date,1,7)
)
-- final aggregation: sum per-customer monthly maxima across customers, excluding NULLs
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(customer_month_max) AS monthly_total_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM per_customer_month_max
WHERE customer_month_max IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

WITH events_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    e.visit_id,
    e.cookie_id,
    e.page_id,
    p.page_name,
    p.product_category,
    p.product_id,
    e.event_type,
    i.event_name,
    e.sequence_number,
    e.event_time
  FROM shopping_cart_events e
  LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
    ON e.page_id = p.page_id
  LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier i
    ON e.event_type = i.event_type
),
-- filter out excluded page_ids and require product_id present
events_filtered AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM events_enriched
  WHERE page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
    AND product_id IS NOT NULL
),
-- per visit+product flags for abandonment/purchase logic
visit_product_flags AS (
  SELECT
    visit_id,
    product_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_add_to_cart,
    MAX(CASE WHEN event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_purchase
  FROM events_filtered
  GROUP BY visit_id, product_id
),
-- aggregate counts per product
product_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    ef.product_id,
    -- get any product_name from hierarchy (could be NULL)
    MAX(ef.page_name) AS product_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ef.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS views_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ef.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ef.event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchases_count,
    -- abandoned: count of visits where had_add_to_cart = 1 and had_purchase = 0
    (
      SELECT COUNT(*) FROM visit_product_flags vpf
      WHERE vpf.product_id = ef.product_id
        AND vpf.had_add_to_cart = 1

    ) AS abandoned_count
  FROM events_filtered ef
  GROUP BY ef.product_id
)

  product_id,
  product_name,
  views_count,
  add_to_cart_count,
  abandoned_count,
  purchases_count

ORDER BY views_count DESC

rows.question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH valid_metrics AS (
  -- filter to desired months and exclude index_value NULL/0
  SELECT
    im._month,
    im._year,
    im.month_year,
    im.interest_id,
    im.composition,
    im.index_value,
    (im.composition / im.index_value) AS metric_ratio
  FROM interest_metrics im
  WHERE im.month_year BETWEEN '09-2018' AND '08-2019'
    AND im.index_value IS NOT NULL
    AND im.index_value != 0
),
-- For each month, pick the interest with the maximum metric_ratio.
-- Tie-break deterministically by smallest interest_id.
monthly_top AS (
  SELECT
    vm.month_year,
    vm._year,
    vm._month,
    vm.interest_id,
    vm.metric_ratio
  FROM valid_metrics vm
  JOIN (
    SELECT
      month_year,
      MAX(metric_ratio) AS max_metric_ratio
    FROM valid_metrics
    GROUP BY month_year
  ) mmax
    ON vm.month_year = mmax.month_year
   AND vm.metric_ratio = mmax.max_metric_ratio
  -- tie-break to a single row per month by choosing smallest interest_id
  GROUP BY vm.month_year
  HAVING vm.interest_id = MIN(vm.interest_id)
),
-- Add previous 1 and 2 months and 3-month rolling average of the monthly maxes.
monthly_with_history AS (
  SELECT
    mt.month_year,
    mt._year,
    mt._month,
    mt.interest_id,
    mt.metric_ratio AS max_index_composition,
    LAG(mt.interest_id, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month) AS prev1_interest_id,
    LAG(mt.metric_ratio, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month) AS prev1_max_index_composition,
    LAG(mt.interest_id, 2) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month) AS prev2_interest_id,
    LAG(mt.metric_ratio, 2) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month) AS prev2_max_index_composition,
    AVG(mt.metric_ratio) OVER (
      ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month
      ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS rolling_avg_3mo
  FROM monthly_top mt
)
SELECT
  mw.month_year AS month,
  cur.interest_name AS interest_name,
  mw.max_index_composition,
  mw.rolling_avg_3mo,
  prev1.interest_name AS prev1_interest_name,
  mw.prev1_max_index_composition,
  prev2.interest_name AS prev2_interest_name,
  mw.prev2_max_index_composition
FROM monthly_with_history mw
LEFT JOIN interest_map cur  ON cur.id = mw.interest_id
LEFT JOIN interest_map prev1 ON prev1.id = mw.prev1_interest_id
LEFT JOIN interest_map prev2 ON prev2.id = mw.prev2_interest_id
ORDER BY mw._year, mw._month

rows.question: Identify the country with data inserted on nine different days in January 2022. Then, find the longest consecutive period with data insertions for this country during January 2022, and calculate the proportion of entries that are from its capital city within this longest consecutive insertion period.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- consider only January 2022 rows
jan_rows AS (
  SELECT
    country_id,
    country_name,
    country_code_2,
    DATE(created_on) AS created_on
  FROM cities_countries
  WHERE DATE(created_on) BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-31'
),
-- countries that have exactly 9 distinct days in January 2022
countries_with_9_days AS (
  SELECT country_name, country_code_2, COUNT(DISTINCT created_on) AS distinct_days
  FROM jan_rows
  GROUP BY country_name, country_code_2
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT created_on) = 9
),
-- per-country distinct dates (to find consecutive runs)
country_dates AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT country_name, country_code_2, created_on
  FROM jan_rows
  WHERE country_name IN (SELECT country_name FROM countries_with_9_days)
),
-- identify consecutive-date groups using row_number trick
country_groups AS (
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code_2,
    created_on,
    DATE(created_on, '-' || (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country_name ORDER BY created_on)) || ' days') AS grp
  FROM country_dates
),
-- compute spans per group
country_spans AS (
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code_2,
    MIN(created_on) AS span_start,
    MAX(created_on) AS span_end,
    CAST((julianday(MAX(created_on)) - julianday(MIN(created_on))) + 1 AS INTEGER) AS span_length
  FROM country_groups
  GROUP BY country_name, country_code_2, grp
),
-- pick the best (longest, tie -> earliest start) span per country
best_spans AS (
  SELECT country_name, country_code_2, span_start, span_end, span_length
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country_name ORDER BY span_length DESC, span_start ASC) AS rn
    FROM country_spans
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
),
-- total rows in cities_countries for the country within that chosen span (within January)
total_rows AS (
  SELECT
    b.country_name,
    COUNT(*) AS rows_in_period_total
  FROM best_spans b
  JOIN cities_countries cc
    ON cc.country_name = b.country_name
   AND DATE(cc.created_on) BETWEEN DATE(b.span_start) AND DATE(b.span_end)
  GROUP BY b.country_name
),
-- capital rows: join to cities where capital = 1 by country_code_2
capital_rows AS (
  SELECT
    b.country_name,
    COUNT(*) AS rows_in_period_capital_count
  FROM best_spans b
  JOIN cities_countries cc
    ON cc.country_name = b.country_name
   AND DATE(cc.created_on) BETWEEN DATE(b.span_start) AND DATE(b.span_end)
  JOIN cities ci
    ON ci.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
   AND ci.capital = 1
  GROUP BY b.country_name
)
SELECT
  b.country_name AS country_name,
  w9.distinct_days AS jan_2022_distinct_insert_days_count,
  DATE(b.span_start) AS longest_consecutive_period_start,
  DATE(b.span_end)   AS longest_consecutive_period_end,
  b.span_length AS longest_consecutive_period_length_days,
  COALESCE(t.rows_in_period_total, 0) AS rows_in_period_total,
  COALESCE(c.rows_in_period_capital_count, 0) AS rows_in_period_capital_count,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t.rows_in_period_total,0) = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE CAST(COALESCE(c.rows_in_period_capital_count,0) AS REAL) / t.rows_in_period_total
  END AS capital_proportion
FROM best_spans b
JOIN countries_with_9_days w9
  ON b.country_name = w9.country_name AND b.country_code_2 = w9.country_code_2
LEFT JOIN total_rows t
  ON b.country_name = t.country_name
LEFT JOIN capital_rows c
  ON b.country_name = c.country_name
ORDER BY b.country_name

rows.question: Calculate the number of new cities inserted in April, May, and June for each year from 2021 to 2023. For each month, compute the cumulative running total of cities added for that specific month across the years up to and including the given year (i.e., sum the counts of that month over the years). Additionally, calculate the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total for each month, comparing each year to the previous year. Present the results only for 2022 and 2023, listing the year, the month, the total number of cities added in that month, the cumulative running total for that month, and the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total. Use the data from 2021 solely as a baseline for calculating growth rates, and exclude it from the final output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cities_monthly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_month,
    CASE strftime('%m', insert_date)
      WHEN '04' THEN 'April'
      WHEN '05' THEN 'May'
      WHEN '06' THEN 'June'
    END AS insert_month_name,
    COUNT(*) AS month_total
  FROM cities
  WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
    AND strftime('%m', insert_date) IN ('04','05','06')
    AND CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2021 AND 2023
  GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
),
running_totals AS (
  SELECT
    c1.insert_year,
    c1.insert_month,
    c1.insert_month_name,
    c1.month_total,
    (SELECT SUM(c2.month_total)
     FROM cities_monthly_counts c2
     WHERE c2.insert_month_name = c1.insert_month_name
       AND c2.insert_year <= c1.insert_year
    ) AS running_total
  FROM cities_monthly_counts c1
)
SELECT
  rt.insert_year AS year,
  rt.insert_month_name AS month,
  rt.month_total,
  rt.running_total,
  CASE
    WHEN prev.month_total IS NULL OR prev.month_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(rt.month_total AS REAL) - prev.month_total) / prev.month_total * 100.0
  END AS month_yoy_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN prev.running_total IS NULL OR prev.running_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(rt.running_total AS REAL) - prev.running_total) / prev.running_total * 100.0
  END AS running_yoy_pct
FROM running_totals rt
LEFT JOIN running_totals prev
  ON prev.insert_month_name = rt.insert_month_name
  AND prev.insert_year = rt.insert_year - 1
WHERE rt.insert_year IN (2022,2023)
ORDER BY rt.insert_year ASC, rt.insert_month ASC

rows.question: Based on the state each female legislator first represented, which state has the highest number of female legislators whose terms included December 31st at any point, and what is that count? Please provide the state's abbreviation.

  SELECT
    lt.id_bioguide,
    lt.term_id AS first_term_id,
    lt.term_start AS first_term_start,
    lt.state AS first_term_state
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  JOIN (
    SELECT id_bioguide, MIN(term_start) AS min_start
    FROM legislators_terms
    WHERE term_start IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY id_bioguide
  ) m ON lt.id_bioguide = m.id_bioguide AND lt.term_start = m.min_start

    lt.id_bioguide,

      CASE

          CASE
            -- check if term_start or term_end is on 12-31 (use '1953-12-31' style month-day check)
            WHEN substr(lt.term_start,6,5) = '12-31' THEN 1
            WHEN substr(lt.term_end,6,5) = '12-31' THEN 1
            -- otherwise, if term_start <= term_end and there exists some year where month-day 12-31 falls between them,

  FROM overtake_with_retire ow
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps_same
    ON ps_same.race_id = ow.race_id
   AND ps_same.driver_id = ow.overtaken_driver_id
   AND ps_same.lap = ow.lap
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps_prev
    ON ps_prev.race_id = ow.race_id

rows.question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE packaging_relations_clean AS (
SELECT
  packaging_id,
  contains_id,
  qty
FROM
  packaging_relations
WHERE
  packaging_id IS NOT NULL
  AND contains_id IS NOT NULL
  AND qty > 0
),
packaging_children_recursive AS (
SELECT
  pr_root.packaging_id AS root_packaging_id,
  pr_leaf.contains_id AS child_packaging_id_leaf,
  pr_leaf.path_qty AS path_qty,
  pr_leaf.path_nodes AS path_nodes
FROM
  (
    SELECT packaging_id, contains_id, qty FROM packaging_relations
    WHERE packaging_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
  ) pr_root,
  (
    WITH RECURSIVE
    rel(packaging_id, contains_id, qty) AS (
      SELECT packaging_id, contains_id, qty FROM packaging_relations
    ),
    -- start from each direct child; path_nodes as comma-separated ids; path_qty cumulative product
    reach(start_id, packaging_id, contains_id, path_qty, path_nodes) AS (
      SELECT packaging_id AS start_id, packaging_id, contains_id, qty AS path_qty, printf('%d,%d', packaging_id, contains_id) AS path_nodes
      FROM rel
      UNION ALL
      SELECT r.start_id, rr.packaging_id, rr.contains_id, (r.path_qty * rr.qty) AS path_qty, (r.path_nodes || ',' || rr.contains_id) AS path_nodes
      FROM reach r
      JOIN rel rr ON rr.packaging_id = r.contains_id
      WHERE instr(r.path_nodes, printf(',%d', rr.contains_id)) = 0
    ),
    -- find leaves: nodes that do not appear as packaging_id in rel (i.e., have no children)
    leaves AS (
      SELECT r.start_id AS root_id, r.contains_id AS leaf_id, r.path_qty AS path_qty, r.path_nodes AS path_nodes
      FROM reach r
      LEFT JOIN rel sub ON sub.packaging_id = r.contains_id
      WHERE sub.packaging_id IS NULL
    )
    SELECT l.root_id AS packaging_id, l.leaf_id AS contains_id, l.path_qty AS path_qty, l.path_nodes AS path_nodes
    FROM leaves l
  ) pr_leaf
WHERE pr_root.packaging_id = pr_leaf.packaging_id
),
packaging_leaf_totals_per_parent AS (
SELECT
  pr.packaging_id AS packaging_id,
  SUM(pcr.path_qty) AS total_leaf_qty
FROM packaging_relations pr
LEFT JOIN packaging_children_recursive pcr
  ON pcr.root_packaging_id = pr.packaging_id
    AND pcr.child_packaging_id_leaf IS NOT NULL
WHERE pr.packaging_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
GROUP BY pr.packaging_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_leaf_qty) AS average_total_qty
FROM packaging_leaf_totals_per_parent
WHERE total_leaf_qty IS NOT NULL

rows.question: Which top-level packaging containers, meaning those not contained within any other packaging, have any item for which the total quantity accumulated across all nested levels in the hierarchy exceeds 500, and what are the names of both these containers and the corresponding items?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
-- clean relations
rel AS (
  SELECT packaging_id, contains_id, qty
  FROM packaging_relations
  WHERE packaging_id IS NOT NULL AND contains_id IS NOT NULL AND qty > 0
),
-- all packaging rows
pkg AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM packaging
),
-- identify top-level packaging (those not appearing as contains_id)
top_levels AS (
  SELECT id AS top_id
  FROM pkg
  WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT contains_id FROM rel)
),
-- recursive traversal: for each top-level start, follow containment edges, carrying cumulative product qty
reach AS (
  -- direct edges from a top-level root
  SELECT
    t.top_id AS root_id,
    r.contains_id AS node_id,
    r.qty AS path_qty,
    printf('%d,%d', t.top_id, r.contains_id) AS path_nodes
  FROM top_levels t
  JOIN rel r ON r.packaging_id = t.top_id

  UNION ALL

  -- extend paths by joining on packaging_id = previous node
  SELECT
    rr.root_id,
    r.contains_id,
    rr.path_qty * r.qty AS path_qty,
    rr.path_nodes || ',' || r.contains_id AS path_nodes
  FROM reach rr
  JOIN rel r ON r.packaging_id = rr.node_id
  -- prevent cycles by ensuring the new node_id is not already in path_nodes
  WHERE instr(rr.path_nodes, ',' || r.contains_id) = 0
),
-- include also direct containment where the top-level might directly contain items (already in reach),
-- and aggregate across all distinct paths from a given top-level to a given item
agg AS (
  SELECT
    root_id AS top_level_packaging_id,
    node_id AS item_packaging_id,
    SUM(path_qty) AS total_accumulated_qty
  FROM reach
  GROUP BY root_id, node_id
)
SELECT
  a.top_level_packaging_id,
  p_top.name AS top_level_packaging_name,
  a.item_packaging_id,
  p_item.name AS item_packaging_name,
  a.total_accumulated_qty
FROM agg a
JOIN pkg p_top ON p_top.id = a.top_level_packaging_id
JOIN pkg p_item ON p_item.id = a.item_packaging_id

next6_sums AS (

),
product_12m_centered_moving_average_windows AS (

    ON pms.product_id = w.product_id AND pms.mth = w.target_mth

  FROM product_minimums

-- monthly purchases summed by product and month (YYYY-MM-01)
purchases_by_product_month AS (
  SELECT
    p.product_id AS product_id,
    substr(p.purchased, 1, 7) || '-01' AS mth,
    SUM(p.qty) AS purchases_qty

monthly_sales_by_product AS (
  SELECT product_id, mth, qty AS sales_qty
  FROM monthly_sales
),
-- compute starting inventory as sum of inventory.qty for inventory rows whose linked purchase.purchased <= 2018-12-31
-- If inventory rows exist without a purchase (purchase_id IS NULL), include them as part of starting inventory (treat as available stock)
start_inv AS (
  SELECT
    pmc.product_id,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(i.qty)
      FROM inventory i
      LEFT JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
      WHERE i.product_id = pmc.product_id
        AND (
          -- include inventory rows whose purchase date is <= year end 2018
          (p.purchased IS NOT NULL AND p.purchased <= '2018-12-31')
          -- or inventory rows with no linked purchase (treat as existing stock)
          OR p.purchased IS NULL
        )
    ), 0.0) AS starting_inventory,
    pmc.qty_minimum,
    pmc.qty_purchase
  FROM product_minimums_catalog pmc
),
-- months to simulate
months(mth, seq) AS (
  VALUES ('2019-01-01', 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(mth, '+1 month'), seq+1 FROM months WHERE seq < 12
),
-- cross join products with months and attach month's purchases and sales
month_data AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_id,
    m.mth,
    COALESCE(ms.sales_qty, 0.0) AS sales_qty,
    COALESCE(pb.purchases_qty, 0.0) AS purchases_qty,
    s.qty_minimum,
    s.qty_purchase,
    s.starting_inventory
  FROM start_inv s
  CROSS JOIN months m
  LEFT JOIN monthly_sales_by_product ms
    ON ms.product_id = s.product_id AND ms.mth = m.mth
  LEFT JOIN purchases_by_product_month pb
    ON pb.product_id = s.product_id AND pb.mth = m.mth
),
-- recursive simulation month by month
rec(product_id, mth, seq, opening_inventory, raw_ending, ending_inventory, qty_minimum, qty_purchase) AS (
  -- base month 2019-01-01
  SELECT
    md.product_id,
    md.mth,
    1 AS seq,
    md.starting_inventory AS opening_inventory,
    (md.starting_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty) AS raw_ending,
    CASE
      WHEN (md.starting_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty) < md.qty_minimum
        THEN (md.starting_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty + md.qty_purchase)
      ELSE (md.starting_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty)
    END AS ending_inventory,
    md.qty_minimum,
    md.qty_purchase
  FROM month_data md
  WHERE md.mth = '2019-01-01'
  UNION ALL
  -- subsequent months: opening is prior ending
  SELECT
    md.product_id,
    md.mth,
    rec.seq + 1,
    rec.ending_inventory AS opening_inventory,
    (rec.ending_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty) AS raw_ending,
    CASE
      WHEN (rec.ending_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty) < rec.qty_minimum
        THEN (rec.ending_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty + rec.qty_purchase)
      ELSE (rec.ending_inventory + md.purchases_qty - md.sales_qty)
    END AS ending_inventory,
    rec.qty_minimum,
    rec.qty_purchase
  FROM rec
  JOIN month_data md
    ON md.product_id = rec.product_id
   AND md.mth = date(rec.mth, '+1 month')
)
-- pick for each product the month with minimal absolute difference; tie -> earliest month
SELECT
  r.product_id,
  r.mth,
  r.abs_diff
FROM (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    mth,
    ABS(ending_inventory - qty_minimum) AS abs_diff,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY ABS(ending_inventory - qty_minimum) ASC, mth ASC) AS rn
  FROM rec
) r
WHERE r.rn = 1
ORDER BY r.product_id ASC

rows.question: Identify the first 10 words, sorted alphabetically, that are 4 to 5 characters long, start with 'r', and have at least one anagram of the same length, considering case-sensitive letters. Provide the count of such anagrams for each word.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH word_list_tokens AS (
  SELECT
    words AS word,
    LENGTH(words) AS length,
    SUBSTR(words, 1, 1) AS first_char,
    (
      SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(ch, '')
      FROM (
        SELECT SUBSTR(words, n, 1) AS ch
        FROM (
          SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER () AS n
          FROM (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1) nums
        )
        WHERE n <= LENGTH(words)
        ORDER BY ch
      )
    ) AS sorted_chars
  FROM word_list
),
word_list_anagram_groups AS (
  SELECT
    sorted_chars,
    length,
    COUNT(*) AS group_count
  FROM word_list_tokens
  GROUP BY sorted_chars, length
)
SELECT
  wlt.word AS word,
  (wag.group_count - 1) AS anagram_count
FROM word_list_tokens wlt
JOIN word_list_anagram_groups wag
  ON wlt.sorted_chars = wag.sorted_chars
  AND wlt.length = wag.length
WHERE wlt.length IN (4,5)
  AND wlt.first_char = 'r'
  AND (wag.group_count - 1) >= 1
ORDER BY wlt.word ASC
LIMIT 10

product_qtr_totals AS (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    prod_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_quarter_id = 1772 THEN product_city_quarter_amount_sold ELSE 0 END) AS total_sales_q4_2019,

  FROM product_city_qtr

selected_cities_qtr_totals AS (

rows.question: What is the average projected monthly sales in USD for France in 2021, considering only product sales with promotions where promo_total_id = 1 and channels where channel_total_id = 1, by taking each product’s monthly sales from 2019 and 2020, calculating the growth rate from 2019 to 2020 for that same product and month, applying this growth rate to project 2021 monthly sales, converting all projected 2021 amounts to USD with the 2021 exchange rates, and finally averaging and listing them by month?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH currency_rates AS (
  SELECT country, year, month, to_us
  FROM currency
),
sales_with_dims AS (
  SELECT
    s.prod_id,
    s.cust_id,
    cu.country_id,
    co.country_name,
    s.promo_id,
    p.promo_total_id,
    s.channel_id,
    ch.channel_total_id,
    s.time_id,
    t.calendar_year,
    t.calendar_month_number,
    s.amount_sold
  FROM sales AS s
  JOIN customers AS cu ON cu.cust_id = s.cust_id
  JOIN countries AS co ON co.country_id = cu.country_id
  JOIN promotions AS p ON p.promo_id = s.promo_id
  JOIN channels AS ch ON ch.channel_id = s.channel_id
  JOIN times AS t ON t.time_id = s.time_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'France'
    AND p.promo_total_id = 1
    AND ch.channel_total_id = 1
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
),
monthly_product_sales_by_year AS (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    calendar_year,
    calendar_month_number,
    SUM(amount_sold) AS sum_amount_sold
  FROM sales_with_dims
  GROUP BY prod_id, calendar_year, calendar_month_number
),
sales_2019 AS (
  SELECT prod_id, calendar_month_number, sum_amount_sold AS sales_2019
  FROM monthly_product_sales_by_year
  WHERE calendar_year = 2019
),
sales_2020 AS (
  SELECT prod_id, calendar_month_number, sum_amount_sold AS sales_2020
  FROM monthly_product_sales_by_year
  WHERE calendar_year = 2020
),
prod_month_pairs AS (
  -- all product-month combinations that appear in either 2019 or 2020
  SELECT prod_id, calendar_month_number FROM sales_2019
  UNION
  SELECT prod_id, calendar_month_number FROM sales_2020
),
proj_local AS (
  SELECT
    pmp.calendar_month_number,
    pmp.prod_id,
    COALESCE(s20.sales_2020, 0.0) AS sales_2020,
    COALESCE(s19.sales_2019, 0.0) AS sales_2019,
    -- compute growth rate per rules: if sales_2019 = 0 then growth = 0
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(s19.sales_2019,0.0) = 0.0 THEN COALESCE(s20.sales_2020, 0.0)  -- projected_2021 = sales_2020
      ELSE COALESCE(s20.sales_2020, 0.0) * (1.0 + (s20.sales_2020 - s19.sales_2019) / s19.sales_2019)
    END AS projected_2021_local
  FROM prod_month_pairs pmp
  LEFT JOIN sales_2019 s19 ON s19.prod_id = pmp.prod_id AND s19.calendar_month_number = pmp.calendar_month_number
  LEFT JOIN sales_2020 s20 ON s20.prod_id = pmp.prod_id AND s20.calendar_month_number = pmp.calendar_month_number
  -- exclude product-months that have no sales in both years (both would be NULL -> not in prod_month_pairs)
),
proj_usd AS (
  SELECT
    pl.calendar_month_number,
    pl.prod_id,
    pl.projected_2021_local,
    cr.to_us,
    pl.projected_2021_local * COALESCE(cr.to_us, 1.0) AS projected_2021_usd
  FROM proj_local pl
  JOIN currency_rates cr
    ON cr.country = 'France'
    AND cr.year = 2021
    AND cr.month = pl.calendar_month_number
)
SELECT
  calendar_month_number AS calendar_month,
  AVG(projected_2021_usd) AS avg_projected_sales_usd
FROM proj_usd
GROUP BY calendar_month_number
ORDER BY calendar_month_number ASC

      ELSE

          CASE

rows.question: Analyze the soccer match dataset to determine the champion team for each season across all countries and leagues, awarding 3 points for every win, 1 point for every tie, and 0 points for every loss. For each season, return the champion’s team name, the league, the country, and the total points accumulated.

WITH matches_cleaned AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM "Match"
  WHERE home_team_goal IS NOT NULL
    AND away_team_goal IS NOT NULL
),
match_team_points AS (
  SELECT
    m.match_api_id,
    m.season,
    m.league_id,
    m.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
    1 AS is_home,
    CASE
      WHEN m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal THEN 3
      WHEN m.home_team_goal = m.away_team_goal THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS points
  FROM matches_cleaned m
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    m.match_api_id,
    m.season,
    m.league_id,
    m.away_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
    0 AS is_home,
    CASE
      WHEN m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 3
      WHEN m.away_team_goal = m.home_team_goal THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS points
  FROM matches_cleaned m
),
team_season_points AS (
  SELECT
    season,
    team_api_id,
    SUM(points) AS total_points
  FROM match_team_points

  SELECT season, MAX(total_points) AS max_points
  FROM team_season_points
  GROUP BY season
)

  l.name AS league_name,
  COALESCE(t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name) AS champion_team_name,
  tsp.total_points AS champion_total_points
FROM team_season_points tsp
JOIN season_max sm
  ON sm.season = tsp.season
  AND sm.max_points = tsp.total_points
JOIN Team t
  ON t.team_api_id = tsp.team_api_id
-- find a league (and thus country) for that team in that season using cleaned matches
JOIN matches_cleaned m

  AND (m.home_team_api_id = tsp.team_api_id OR m.away_team_api_id = tsp.team_api_id)
JOIN League l
  ON l.id = m.league_id

  ON c.id = l.country_id

GROUP BY
  tsp.season,
  c.name,
  l.name,
  champion_team_name,
  tsp.total_points
ORDER BY
  tsp.season ASC,

rows.question: Can you calculate the 5-day symmetric moving average of predicted toy sales for December 5 to 8, 2018, using daily sales data from January 1, 2017, to August 29, 2018, with a simple linear regression model? Finally provide the sum of those four 5-day moving averages?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH orders_with_purchase_date AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    substr(o.order_purchase_timestamp, 1, 10) AS order_purchase_date,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_status
  FROM orders o
),
order_items_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    oi.*,
    o.order_purchase_date,
    p.product_category_name,
    t.product_category_name_english
  FROM order_items oi
  LEFT JOIN orders_with_purchase_date o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
),
daily_sales AS (
  SELECT
    date(order_purchase_date) AS dt,
    CAST(julianday(date(order_purchase_date)) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS x,
    COUNT(*) AS y
  FROM order_items_enriched
  WHERE (product_category_name = 'toys' OR product_category_name_english = 'toys')
    AND date(order_purchase_date) BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2018-08-29'
  GROUP BY date(order_purchase_date)
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(x) AS mean_x,
    AVG(y) AS mean_y,
    (AVG(x * y) - AVG(x) * AVG(y)) AS cov_xy,
    (AVG(x * x) - AVG(x) * AVG(x)) AS var_x
  FROM daily_sales
),
model AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN var_x = 0 OR var_x IS NULL THEN 0.0 ELSE cov_xy / var_x END AS slope,
    (mean_y - (CASE WHEN var_x = 0 OR var_x IS NULL THEN 0.0 ELSE cov_xy / var_x END) * mean_x) AS intercept
  FROM stats
),
targets AS (
  SELECT '2018-12-05' AS predicted_date UNION ALL
  SELECT '2018-12-06' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2018-12-07' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2018-12-08'
),
preds AS (
  SELECT
    t.predicted_date,
    m.intercept + m.slope * CAST(julianday(t.predicted_date) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS center_pred,
    m.intercept + m.slope * CAST(julianday(date(t.predicted_date, '-2 days')) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS pred_m2,
    m.intercept + m.slope * CAST(julianday(date(t.predicted_date, '-1 day')) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS pred_m1,
    m.intercept + m.slope * CAST(julianday(date(t.predicted_date, '+1 day')) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS pred_p1,
    m.intercept + m.slope * CAST(julianday(date(t.predicted_date, '+2 days')) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS pred_p2
  FROM targets t CROSS JOIN model m
),
sums AS (
  SELECT SUM((pred_m2 + pred_m1 + center_pred + pred_p1 + pred_p2) / 5.0) AS sum_of_the_four_5_day_moving_averages
  FROM preds
)
SELECT
  p.predicted_date,
  ROUND(p.center_pred, 6) AS predicted_sales,
  ROUND((p.pred_m2 + p.pred_m1 + p.center_pred + p.pred_p1 + p.pred_p2) / 5.0, 6) AS five_day_symmetric_moving_average,
  ROUND(s.sum_of_the_four_5_day_moving_averages, 6) AS sum_of_the_four_5_day_moving_averages
FROM preds p CROSS JOIN sums s

Use the customer unique identifier. Clearly define how to calculate Recency based on the latest purchase timestamp and specify the criteria for classifying RFM segments. The average sales should be computed as the total spend divided by the total number of orders. Please analyze and report the differences in average sales across the RFM segments

WITH orders_delivered AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM orders
  WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
),
order_payments_sum AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS payments_total
  FROM order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
order_items_sum AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(price + COALESCE(freight_value,0)) AS items_total
  FROM order_items

order_totals_union AS (
  SELECT oi.order_id, COALESCE(op.payments_total, oi.items_total, 0.0) AS order_total
  FROM order_items_sum oi
  LEFT JOIN order_payments_sum op ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
  UNION
  SELECT op.order_id, COALESCE(op.payments_total, oi.items_total, 0.0) AS order_total
  FROM order_payments_sum op
  LEFT JOIN order_items_sum oi ON oi.order_id = op.order_id
  WHERE oi.order_id IS NULL
),
customer_orders AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_unique_id,
    o.order_id,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp,
    ot.order_total
  FROM orders_delivered o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  LEFT JOIN order_totals_union ot ON o.order_id = ot.order_id
  WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL
),
ref AS (
  -- reference date for recency = latest purchase timestamp among delivered orders
  SELECT MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS ref_date FROM customer_orders
),
customer_rfm AS (
  SELECT
    co.customer_unique_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT co.order_id) AS frequency,
    SUM(COALESCE(co.order_total,0.0)) AS total_spend,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT co.order_id)=0 THEN 0.0 ELSE SUM(COALESCE(co.order_total,0.0))*1.0/COUNT(DISTINCT co.order_id) END AS avg_sales_per_order,
    -- Recency in days: difference between reference (most recent purchase in dataset) and customer's last purchase
    (julianday((SELECT ref_date FROM ref)) - julianday(MAX(co.order_purchase_timestamp))) AS recency_days,
    MAX(co.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_purchase
  FROM customer_orders co
  GROUP BY co.customer_unique_id
),
-- score R,F,M into 5 buckets each using NTILE(5)
rfm_ranks AS (
  SELECT
    customer_unique_id,
    recency_days,
    frequency,
    total_spend,
    avg_sales_per_order,
    NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY recency_days) AS r_tile,           -- lower recency_days -> more recent -> lower R score (1 = most recent)
    NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS f_tile,         -- higher frequency -> better -> F score 1 = most frequent
    NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY total_spend DESC) AS m_tile        -- higher spend -> better -> M score 1 = highest spend
  FROM customer_rfm
),
scored AS (
  SELECT
    customer_unique_id,
    recency_days,
    frequency,
    total_spend,
    avg_sales_per_order,
    r_tile AS R_score,
    f_tile AS F_score,
    m_tile AS M_score
  FROM rfm_ranks
)
SELECT
  R_score,
  F_score,
  M_score,
  (CAST(R_score AS TEXT) || CAST(F_score AS TEXT) || CAST(M_score AS TEXT)) AS rfm_segment,
  COUNT(*) AS customers_in_segment,
  ROUND(AVG(avg_sales_per_order), 2) AS avg_sales_per_order, -- average across customers of their avg sales per order
  ROUND(SUM(total_spend) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(frequency),0), 2) AS overall_avg_sales_per_order_in_segment, -- total spend / total orders in segment
  ROUND(AVG(total_spend), 2) AS avg_total_spend_per_customer,
  ROUND(AVG(frequency), 2) AS avg_total_orders_per_customer,
  ROUND(AVG(recency_days), 2) AS avg_recency_days
FROM scored
GROUP BY R_score, F_score, M_score
ORDER BY R_score, F_score, M_score

  FROM invoices

rows.question: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and version) that occurs most frequently for each status ('strong' or 'soft'), along with the number of times it occurs. A model has a 'strong' status if, for any of its steps, the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models is less than the 'Stack' model's test score. It has a 'soft' status if the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models equals the 'Stack' model's test score. Count how many times each L1_model is associated with a 'strong' or 'soft' status across all models, and determine which L1_model has the highest occurrence for each status.

WITH models_with_l1 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT name, version, L1_model
  FROM model
),
-- compute per (name,version,step) the stack score (if any) and max non-stack test_score (if any)
scores_by_step AS (
  SELECT
    ms.name,
    ms.version,
    ms.step,
    MAX(CASE WHEN ms.model = 'Stack' THEN ms.test_score END) AS stack_score,
    MAX(CASE WHEN ms.model != 'Stack' THEN ms.test_score END) AS max_nonstack_test_score
  FROM model_score ms
  GROUP BY ms.name, ms.version, ms.step
),
-- keep only steps that have a Stack row (stack_score IS NOT NULL)
steps_with_stack AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM scores_by_step
  WHERE stack_score IS NOT NULL
),
-- determine per (name,version) whether any step makes it strong and/or soft
model_status_by_version AS (
  SELECT
    name,
    version,
    MAX(CASE WHEN max_nonstack_test_score < stack_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_strong,
    MAX(CASE WHEN max_nonstack_test_score = stack_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_soft
  FROM steps_with_stack
  GROUP BY name, version
),
-- counts per L1_model
counts_per_l1 AS (
  SELECT
    m.L1_model,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.is_strong = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS strong_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.is_soft = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS soft_count
  FROM models_with_l1 m
  JOIN model_status_by_version s USING(name, version)
  GROUP BY m.L1_model
),
-- determine max counts for strong and soft
max_counts AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT MAX(strong_count) FROM counts_per_l1) AS max_strong,
    (SELECT MAX(soft_count) FROM counts_per_l1) AS max_soft
)
SELECT
  c.L1_model,
  c.strong_count,
  c.soft_count,
  -- top_strong_L1_model: all L1_models tied for max_strong
  (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(L1_model, ',')
   FROM counts_per_l1
   WHERE strong_count = mc.max_strong) AS top_strong_L1_model,
  -- top_soft_L1_model: all L1_models tied for max_soft
  (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(L1_model, ',')
   FROM counts_per_l1
   WHERE soft_count = mc.max_soft) AS top_soft_L1_model
FROM counts_per_l1 c
CROSS JOIN max_counts mc
ORDER BY c.strong_count DESC, c.soft_count DESC

    f.aircraft_code,
    f.actual_departure,
    f.actual_arrival
  FROM flights f
  WHERE f.departure_airport IS NOT NULL
    AND f.arrival_airport IS NOT NULL
),
per_flight AS (
  -- compute per-flight distances and canonical unordered city pair
  SELECT
    -- canonicalize city names so pair is unordered
    CASE
      WHEN dep.city_en <= arr.city_en THEN dep.city_en
      ELSE arr.city_en
    END AS city1,
    CASE
      WHEN dep.city_en <= arr.city_en THEN arr.city_en
      ELSE dep.city_en
    END AS city2,
    2.0 * 6371.0 * ASIN(
      SQRT(
        POWER(SIN(RADIANS((COALESCE(arr.latitude,0.0) - COALESCE(dep.latitude,0.0)) / 2.0)), 2)
        + COS(RADIANS(COALESCE(dep.latitude,0.0))) * COS(RADIANS(COALESCE(arr.latitude,0.0)))
          * POWER(SIN(RADIANS((COALESCE(arr.longitude,0.0) - COALESCE(dep.longitude,0.0)) / 2.0)), 2)
      )
    ) AS distance_km
  FROM flights_filtered_valid_airports f
  JOIN airports_core dep ON f.departure_airport = dep.airport_code
  JOIN airports_core arr ON f.arrival_airport = arr.airport_code
  WHERE dep.city_en IS NOT NULL
    AND arr.city_en IS NOT NULL
    AND dep.city_en <> arr.city_en
    -- ensure numeric coords exist
    AND dep.latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND dep.longitude IS NOT NULL
    AND arr.latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND arr.longitude IS NOT NULL
),
per_pair_avg AS (
  -- average distance per unordered city pair
  SELECT
    city1,
    city2,
    AVG(distance_km) AS avg_d
  FROM per_flight
  GROUP BY city1, city2
),
buckets AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN avg_d >= 0 AND avg_d < 1000 THEN '0'
      WHEN avg_d >= 1000 AND avg_d < 2000 THEN '1000'
      WHEN avg_d >= 2000 AND avg_d < 3000 THEN '2000'
      WHEN avg_d >= 3000 AND avg_d < 4000 THEN '3000'
      WHEN avg_d >= 4000 AND avg_d < 5000 THEN '4000'
      WHEN avg_d >= 5000 AND avg_d < 6000 THEN '5000'
      ELSE '6000+'
    END AS range_label,
    COUNT(*) AS pair_count
  FROM per_pair_avg
  GROUP BY range_label
),
min_bucket AS (
  SELECT range_label AS min_range_label, pair_count AS min_pair_count
  FROM buckets
  ORDER BY pair_count ASC, range_label ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  b.range_label,
  b.pair_count,
  m.min_range_label,
  m.min_pair_count
FROM (
  -- ensure all bins appear even if count = 0
  SELECT '0' AS range_label UNION ALL
  SELECT '1000' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2000' UNION ALL
  SELECT '3000' UNION ALL
  SELECT '4000' UNION ALL
  SELECT '5000' UNION ALL
  SELECT '6000+'
) bin_list
LEFT JOIN buckets b USING (range_label)
CROSS JOIN min_bucket m
ORDER BY
  CASE bin_list.range_label
    WHEN '0' THEN 1 WHEN '1000' THEN 2 WHEN '2000' THEN 3 WHEN '3000' THEN 4
    WHEN '4000' THEN 5 WHEN '5000' THEN 6 ELSE 7 END

rows.question: For the NXT title that had the shortest match (excluding titles with "title change"), what were the names of the two wrestlers involved?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH matches_with_titles_and_duration AS (
  SELECT
    m.id AS match_id,
    m.card_id AS card_id,
    m.title_id AS title_id,
    b.name AS title_name,
    m.duration AS duration,
    COALESCE(m.title_change,0) AS title_change,
    m.winner_id AS winner_id,
    m.loser_id AS loser_id
  FROM Matches m
  LEFT JOIN Belts b ON CAST(m.title_id AS INTEGER) = b.id
),
wrestler_id_name AS (
  SELECT id AS wrestler_id, TRIM(name) AS wrestler_name FROM Wrestlers
),
parsed AS (
  SELECT
    m.*,
    instr(m.duration, ':') AS first_colon,
    -- estimate last colon position: find last ':' by searching for ':' in the substring after the first colon,
    -- if none found, last_colon_pos = first_colon; else compute position relative to full string
    CASE
      WHEN instr(m.duration, ':') = 0 THEN 0
      WHEN instr(substr(m.duration, instr(m.duration, ':') + 1), ':') = 0 THEN instr(m.duration, ':')
      ELSE instr(m.duration, ':') + instr(substr(m.duration, instr(m.duration, ':') + 1), ':')
    END AS last_colon_pos
  FROM matches_with_titles_and_duration m
  WHERE m.duration IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(m.duration) <> ''
    AND LOWER(COALESCE(m.title_name,'') ) LIKE '%nxt%'
    AND m.title_change = 0
),
computed AS (
  SELECT
    p.*,
    (CASE WHEN p.first_colon > 0 AND p.first_colon = p.last_colon_pos THEN 1
          WHEN p.first_colon > 0 AND p.first_colon < p.last_colon_pos THEN 2
          ELSE 0 END) AS colon_count,
    (CASE
      WHEN p.first_colon > 0 AND p.first_colon = p.last_colon_pos THEN
        (CAST(TRIM(substr(p.duration, 1, p.first_colon - 1)) AS INTEGER) * 60)
        + CAST(TRIM(substr(p.duration, p.first_colon + 1)) AS INTEGER)
      WHEN p.first_colon > 0 AND p.first_colon < p.last_colon_pos THEN
        (CAST(TRIM(substr(p.duration, 1, p.first_colon - 1)) AS INTEGER) * 3600)
        + (CAST(TRIM(substr(p.duration, p.first_colon + 1, p.last_colon_pos - p.first_colon - 1)) AS INTEGER) * 60)
        + CAST(TRIM(substr(p.duration, p.last_colon_pos + 1)) AS INTEGER)
      ELSE
        NULL
    END) AS total_seconds
  FROM parsed p
)
SELECT
  w_winner.wrestler_name AS winner_name,
  w_loser.wrestler_name AS loser_name,
  c.duration,
  c.match_id,
  c.card_id
FROM computed c
JOIN wrestler_id_name w_winner ON CAST(w_winner.wrestler_id AS TEXT) = CAST(c.winner_id AS TEXT)
JOIN wrestler_id_name w_loser  ON CAST(w_loser.wrestler_id  AS TEXT) = CAST(c.loser_id  AS TEXT)
WHERE c.total_seconds IS NOT NULL
  AND c.total_seconds = (
    SELECT MIN(total_seconds) FROM computed WHERE total_seconds IS NOT NULL
  )
ORDER BY c.match_id

rows.question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH track_stats AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(Milliseconds) AS global_min_millis,
    AVG(Milliseconds) AS global_avg_millis,
    MAX(Milliseconds) AS global_max_millis
  FROM Track
),
bounds AS (
  SELECT
    global_min_millis,
    global_avg_millis,
    global_max_millis,
    (global_min_millis + global_avg_millis) / 2.0 AS short_upper,
    (global_avg_millis + global_max_millis) / 2.0 AS medium_upper
  FROM track_stats
),
tracks_categorized AS (
  SELECT
    t.TrackId,
    t.Milliseconds,
    t.UnitPrice,
    CASE
      WHEN t.Milliseconds IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN t.Milliseconds >= b.global_min_millis AND t.Milliseconds < b.short_upper THEN 'short'
      WHEN t.Milliseconds >= b.short_upper AND t.Milliseconds < b.medium_upper THEN 'medium'
      WHEN t.Milliseconds >= b.medium_upper AND t.Milliseconds <= b.global_max_millis THEN 'long'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS Category
  FROM Track t
  CROSS JOIN bounds b
)
SELECT
  Category,
  MIN(Milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS MinDurationMinutes,
  MAX(Milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS MaxDurationMinutes,

FROM tracks_categorized
WHERE Category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY Category
ORDER BY CASE Category WHEN 'short' THEN 1 WHEN 'medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'long' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END

    CASE WHEN trim(order_purchase_timestamp) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_purchase_timestamp END AS order_purchase_timestamp_parsed,
    CASE WHEN trim(order_approved_at) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_approved_at END AS order_approved_at_parsed,
    CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_carrier_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_carrier_date END AS order_delivered_carrier_date_parsed,
    CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_customer_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_customer_date END AS order_delivered_customer_date_parsed,
    CASE WHEN trim(order_estimated_delivery_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_estimated_delivery_date END AS order_estimated_delivery_date_parsed
  FROM orders
),
order_items_base AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    order_item_id,
    product_id,
    seller_id,
    shipping_limit_date,
    price,
    freight_value,
    CASE WHEN trim(shipping_limit_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE shipping_limit_date END AS shipping_limit_date_parsed
  FROM order_items
),
products_with_category_en AS (
  SELECT
    p.product_id,
    p.product_category_name,
    t.product_category_name_english,
    p.product_name_lenght,
    p.product_description_lenght,
    p.product_photos_qty,
    p.product_weight_g,
    p.product_length_cm,
    p.product_height_cm,
    p.product_width_cm
  FROM products p
  LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
),
-- Keep latest review per order to avoid double-counting multiple reviews for same order
latest_review_per_order AS (
  SELECT
    review_id,
    order_id,
    review_score,
    review_comment_title,
    review_comment_message,
    review_creation_date,
    review_answer_timestamp
  FROM (
    SELECT
      r.*,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY review_creation_date DESC, review_id DESC) AS rn
    FROM order_reviews r
  ) sub WHERE rn = 1
),
-- Seller-level sales aggregates
seller_item_sales AS (
  SELECT
    oi.seller_id AS seller_id,
    SUM(COALESCE(oi.price,0.0)) AS total_sales,
    COUNT(*) AS total_quantity_sold,
    AVG(oi.price) AS average_item_price
  FROM order_items_base oi
  GROUP BY oi.seller_id
),
-- Counts per seller x product category (to pick top category)
seller_product_category_counts AS (
  SELECT
    oi.seller_id AS seller_id,
    p.product_category_name AS product_category_name,
    p.product_category_name_english AS product_category_name_english,
    COUNT(*) AS category_items_sold_count
  FROM order_items_base oi
  LEFT JOIN products_with_category_en p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY
    oi.seller_id,
    p.product_category_name,
    p.product_category_name_english
),
-- For each seller-order, attach review (if any) and packing time in days
seller_order_review_and_packing AS (
  SELECT
    oi.seller_id AS seller_id,
    o.order_id AS order_id,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp_parsed AS order_purchase_timestamp,
    o.order_delivered_customer_date_parsed AS order_delivered_customer_date,
    lr.review_id AS review_id,
    lr.review_score AS review_score,
    CASE
      WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp_parsed IS NOT NULL
       AND o.order_delivered_customer_date_parsed IS NOT NULL
      THEN (julianday(o.order_delivered_customer_date_parsed) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp_parsed))
      ELSE NULL
    END AS packing_time_days
  FROM order_items_base oi
  JOIN orders_base o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN latest_review_per_order lr
    ON o.order_id = lr.order_id
  GROUP BY oi.seller_id, o.order_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp_parsed, o.order_delivered_customer_date_parsed, lr.review_id, lr.review_score
),
-- Choose a single top category per seller (highest count, tie-breaker by minimal english name)
top_category_per_seller AS (
  SELECT pc.seller_id, pc.product_category_name_english, pc.category_items_sold_count
  FROM seller_product_category_counts pc
  JOIN (
    SELECT seller_id, MAX(category_items_sold_count) AS max_count
    FROM seller_product_category_counts
    GROUP BY seller_id
  ) mx
    ON pc.seller_id = mx.seller_id
   AND pc.category_items_sold_count = mx.max_count
  WHERE pc.product_category_name_english = (
    SELECT MIN(COALESCE(spc2.product_category_name_english, ''))
    FROM seller_product_category_counts spc2
    WHERE spc2.seller_id = pc.seller_id
      AND spc2.category_items_sold_count = pc.category_items_sold_count
  )
)
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  sis.total_sales,
  sis.total_quantity_sold,
  sis.average_item_price,
  avr.avg_review_score AS average_review_score,
  avr.avg_packing_time_days AS average_packing_time_days,
  topcat.product_category_name_english AS top_product_category_english,
  topcat.category_items_sold_count AS top_category_quantity
FROM sellers s
JOIN seller_item_sales sis
  ON sis.seller_id = s.seller_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    AVG(CASE WHEN review_score IS NOT NULL THEN review_score END) AS avg_review_score,
    AVG(CASE WHEN packing_time_days IS NOT NULL THEN packing_time_days END) AS avg_packing_time_days
  FROM seller_order_review_and_packing
  GROUP BY seller_id
) avr
  ON avr.seller_id = s.seller_id
LEFT JOIN top_category_per_seller topcat
  ON topcat.seller_id = s.seller_id
WHERE sis.total_quantity_sold > 100
ORDER BY sis.total_sales DESC
